correctness.rationale: The maximum and runner-up, including their equality classes, are correct. Invertibility makes the squares linearly independent; the zero mixed products of two image basis vectors then force disjoint coordinate supports, so the automorphisms are monomial. Any nonzero determinant summand gives a cycle cover, and on an ℓ-cycle the cover equations give C_(2^ℓ−1). Together with the graph stabilizer this bounds the automorphism order. An exact hand replay, not dependent on re-running the census, separates primes in D: 31 forces the five-cycle (distinct nonidentity labels, each with unique squared successor), giving 31·5; 5 forces the four-cycle and one loop, giving at most 15·4; 7 forces an isolated three-cycle, leaving two vertices, hence at most 21·6. For 126, D must have order 21 and the separate two-vertex support must have a nontrivial order-three diagonal, whose two inverse nonidentity labels force exactly the two opposite arrows. If only 3 divides |D|, order 3 gives m vertices at each of the inverse labels (m=1 or 2, by the cover); graph permutations normalize D, so their order is at most 2(m!)²(5−2m)! ≤12. Order 9 requires all cover diagonals of type 2+2+1, and their distinct coordinate characters force exactly that support (graph group order 8). Trivial D gives at most 120. On a cover-only support weights normalize by successively rescaling and taking a nonzero complex (2^ℓ−1)-st root. Rotations lift for the normalized supports: 31·5 and 3·7·2·3 are attained; the C5 rotation gives the stated nontrivial split action. Multiplying a nonzero ideal element by a suitable basis vector and repeatedly squaring proves the five-cycle is simple.
residual_risks: Reviewed the logic of the packaged census; did not rerun uploaded programs or independently attest incidental census counts. The prime-case proof is a complete replay of the theorem over C without those counts.

originality.rationale: The prior October 25 Resultary finding proves the identical maximum, equality class, extremal group and conjecture corollaries, and its case inequalities and explicit forced supports already imply the entire purported runner-up result. In its order-seven case equality 126 needs |D|=21 (graph order at most 6), hence an order-three diagonal on the complementary two vertices. Such a diagonal on two cover vertices forces the directed two-cycle without loops. The prior three-cycle isolation then leaves exactly C2 plus C3; applying its cycle weight normalization to each component gives uniqueness, and the two independent rotations and root factors give 126. This is a direct equality specialization of the prior proof, not unresolved just because it was not packaged as a separate theorem.
